title: Admin clicks Employees in the side navigation
trigger: Click on the 'Employees' link in the rail (desktop) or Menu (mobile)

nodes.label: Click 'Employees'
nodes.does: Rail navigation renders one link per built section; the user clicks Employees (href /employees).

nodes.label: Client navigation
nodes.does: next/link performs a client-side navigation and requests the RSC payload for /employees (the session cookie travels with it).

nodes.label: Proxy cookie check
nodes.does: Optimistic check only: no session cookie redirects to /sign-in; a present cookie is passed through to be verified by the backend.

nodes.label: /employees page
nodes.does: Route segment; streams a static directory skeleton inside Suspense while the data component loads.

nodes.label: EmployeesDirectory (Server Component)
nodes.does: Loads session and token, parses the URL, then calls the API in parallel (options and the employee page) and picks the page state.

nodes.label: Session cookie and token
nodes.does: Reads the httpOnly session cookie on the server (readSessionToken) and resolves the session; the JWT never reaches browser JavaScript.

nodes.label: resolveSession
nodes.does: Asks the backend who the token belongs to (GET /auth/me) and keeps only display name, role, and scopes.

nodes.label: parseDirectoryQuery
nodes.does: Validates URL search params into a DirectoryQuery; invalid params mean no backend call for the list.

nodes.label: api().listEmployees
nodes.does: Builds GET /api/v1/employees with the query string and the response validator isDirectoryResponse.

nodes.label: fetch to Express
nodes.does: Server-side fetch with Authorization: Bearer <token>, cache no-store, redirect error, and a timeout.

nodes.label: requestLog
nodes.does: Assigns the request ID and logs method, path, status, and duration (no bodies).

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/auth/me
nodes.does: Returns the current user, scopes, and session expiry as CurrentUserResponse.

nodes.label: requireAuth
nodes.does: Reads the Bearer token and puts the freshly loaded principal in res.locals; any auth failure becomes 401 UNAUTHENTICATED.

nodes.label: auth.authenticate
nodes.does: Verifies the HS256 JWT, then reloads the session, user status, role, and scopes from MySQL on every request.

nodes.label: hr_sessions
nodes.does: Session row for the JWT session ID: expiry and revocation.

nodes.label: hr_users
nodes.does: The HR user joined to the session: email, display name, role, status (inactive users are rejected).

nodes.label: hr_user_country_scopes
nodes.does: Countries this HR user may see.

nodes.label: hr_user_department_scopes
nodes.does: Departments this HR user may see (joined to departments for names).

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/employees
nodes.does: Directory list route: no-store, requireAuth, validate, call the service, validate the response.

nodes.label: DirectoryQueryParams (Zod)
nodes.does: Strict query schema (q, filters, sort, page, pageSize ≤ 100); failure is 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

nodes.label: directory.list
nodes.does: Runs the page query and the count query, maps rows to DirectoryRow with selected compensation and USD context.

nodes.label: buildListQueries
nodes.does: Builds parameterised SELECT and COUNT SQL: WHERE (scope AND filters), ORDER BY, LIMIT/OFFSET.

nodes.label: scopeCondition
nodes.does: Turns the principal into a WHERE fragment: ADMIN → TRUE; SCOPED → country IN (…) AND department IN (…); anything else → FALSE.
nodes.scopeRule: This is where Rohan's view is limited: e.country_code IN ('IN') AND d.name IN ('Support','Tech') inside the SQL, so rows, counts, and pages are all scoped.

nodes.label: employees
nodes.does: Employee rows (FROM_EMPLOYEES).

nodes.label: job_titles
nodes.does: Job title and level for each employee.

nodes.label: departments
nodes.does: Department name (used by the scope rule and filters).

nodes.label: compensation_records
nodes.does: LATERAL join picks the selected (current, upcoming, or last) compensation record as of today.

nodes.label: DirectoryResponse.parse
nodes.does: The backend validates its own output against the contract before res.json.

nodes.label: isDirectoryResponse (Ajv)
nodes.does: Next server validates the JSON against the generated OpenAPI schema; a mismatch is INVALID_RESPONSE and no data is shown.

nodes.label: DirectoryResults
nodes.does: Server-renders the table (desktop) or ruled list (mobile) with native-currency money and the rate note.

nodes.label: Browser shows the page
nodes.does: Client component the streamed RSC payload is committed into; later filter and page changes run as router transitions here.

edges.label: SELECT s.expires_at, s.revoked_at … FROM hr_sessions s
JOIN hr_users u ON u.id = s.hr_user_id
SELECT d.name FROM hr_user_department_scopes JOIN departments
request<DirectoryResponse>(spec)
edges.payload: { q, department, country, status, sort, direction, page, pageSize }

edges.label: requireAuth(auth) (principal reloaded again from MySQL, steps 10–13)
pool.query(rows.sql): SELECT … FROM employees e … WHERE scope AND filters ORDER BY … LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
JOIN job_titles jt ON jt.id = e.job_title_id
JOIN departments d ON d.id = jt.department_id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (… FROM compensation_records c …)
pool.query(count.sql) then map rows; return DirectoryResponse
RSC payload streamed to the browser

alternatives.label: Scoped HR (Rohan)
alternatives.condition: principal.role = SCOPED with countries [IN] and departments [Support, Tech]
alternatives.result: The WHERE clause adds e.country_code IN (?) AND d.name IN (?): Rohan's page, total count, and pagination include only India Support and Tech employees. Nothing is filtered in the browser.

alternatives.label: Expired or revoked session
alternatives.condition: authenticate throws (session expired, revoked, user inactive, bad JWT)
alternatives.result: Express returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; the client maps it to kind UNAUTHENTICATED, requireUser/redirectIfUnauthenticated redirect to /session/expired, which clears the cookie.

alternatives.label: No session cookie
alternatives.result: The proxy redirects to /sign-in before any Server Component or backend call runs.

notes: EmployeesDirectory also calls getDirectoryOptions (GET /api/v1/employee-directory/options) in parallel; it follows the same requireAuth path and is not drawn.
requireAuth runs on every backend request, so the principal is reloaded from MySQL twice in this flow (for /auth/me and for /employees).
